title: ParsedPart: all fields pub with no constructor allows callers to build inconsistent body_range → decode_body_value UB
description:
## Problem

`mime-tree/src/part.rs` defines `ParsedPart` with all fields `pub` and no constructor:

```rust
pub struct ParsedPart {
    pub part_id: String,
    pub content_type: String,
    ...
    pub body_range: (u32, u32),
    ...
}
```

The invariant 'body_range indexes into the same `raw` buffer that will be passed to `decode_body_value(raw, part, ...)`' is not enforced and cannot be enforced without a constructor that takes `raw` at construction time.

Callers can legally write:

```rust
let part = ParsedPart {
    body_range: (1_000_000, 50),  // points nowhere sensible
    ...
};
decode_body_value(some_other_raw, &part, None)  // range mismatch
```

## What happens

`decode_body_value` in `mime-tree/src/decode.rs` slices `raw` using `body_range` and returns `ParseError::InvalidRange` if the range is out of bounds, which is safe. However:

1. The error type gives no indication that the range came from a different buffer than intended.
2. Callers who store `ParsedPart` (which is `Serialize + Deserialize`) and later pass it alongside a different `raw` buffer get silent wrong results (range happens to be in-bounds for the wrong buffer) or the `InvalidRange` error — neither communicates the root cause.
3. The scan functions `scan_inline_uuencode` and `scan_inline_yencode` carry the same invariant but enforce it with the same silent-bounds-check approach.

## What goes wrong if left as-is

A common pattern in JMAP/IMAP systems is to store the `ParsedMessage` at parse time and re-fetch the raw bytes later from a blob store for decode. If the raw bytes change between parse and decode (e.g. a re-fetch returns differently-encoded bytes), the mismatch is undetectable. The API contract that `raw` must be the same buffer is implicit and undocumented.

## Files

- `mime-tree/src/part.rs` — `ParsedPart` struct definition
- `mime-tree/src/decode.rs` — `decode_body_value`
- `mime-tree/src/uuencode.rs`, `mime-tree/src/yenc.rs` — scan functions with same invariant
close_reason: Resolved by #[non_exhaustive] added in MIME-8zt.19. External callers can no longer construct ParsedPart with struct literal syntax.
